preamble: Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension  |  100-Point Adverse Prognostic Score  |  ESC/ERS 2022 PH Guidelines / AHA/ATS 2022 PAH Scientific Statement / REVEAL 2.0 Risk Score  |  Progression Trajectory: Fast / Moderate / Slow

questions.question: Is there RV systolic dysfunction (TAPSE <18 mm or RV S' <9.5 cm/s on echo) or clinical right heart failure (elevated JVP, ascites, peripheral edema)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — RV failure confirmed; the single strongest predictor of mortality in PAH; parenteral prostacyclin therapy (epoprostenol or treprostinil) required; lung transplant evaluation

questions.question: Is pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) ≥5 Wood units on right heart catheterization?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severely elevated PVR confirmed; high-risk hemodynamic profile per ESC/ERS; associated with poor response to oral therapy alone; combination therapy + prostacyclin pathway agent required

questions.question: Is cardiac index <2.0 L/min/m² on RHC or estimated severely reduced by echo (IVC dilation, poor CO)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — critically reduced cardiac output confirmed; high-risk marker per REVEAL 2.0; IV/SC prostacyclin escalation required; urgent transplant evaluation if refractory

questions.question: Is the patient in WHO Functional Class III or IV despite PAH-targeted therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — WHO FC III/IV on therapy confirmed; high-risk marker per ESC/ERS and REVEAL 2.0; therapy escalation to triple combination or prostacyclin analog mandatory

questions.question: Is 6MWD <165 meters (high risk) or <440 meters (intermediate risk) on serial testing, or declining >15% between visits?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — significantly reduced or declining 6MWD confirmed; strong independent predictor of mortality; goal is 6MWD >440 m and stable/improving trajectory on therapy

questions.question: Is there a history of syncope or pre-syncope with exertion or at rest?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — exertional syncope confirmed; reflects critically reduced cardiac output reserve; high-risk classification; immediate therapy escalation and hospitalization consideration

questions.question: Is NT-proBNP >1100 pg/mL (high risk) or >300 pg/mL (intermediate risk) on therapy, or rising on serial measurement?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — elevated NT-proBNP on therapy confirmed; ESC/ERS high-risk threshold >1100 pg/mL; rising BNP/NT-proBNP despite therapy is an urgent indicator for escalation

questions.question: Is uric acid >7 mg/dL, creatinine rising, or are there signs of hepatic congestion (elevated bilirubin, ascites) on labs?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — end-organ dysfunction from chronic low cardiac output confirmed; indicates advanced RV failure and systemic venous hypertension; high-risk per REVEAL 2.0

questions.question: Is RV:LV end-diastolic area ratio >1.0, or is there persistent D-shaped LV (eccentricity index >1.1) on echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — severe RV dilation with LV compression confirmed; indicates markedly elevated RV afterload; associated with rapid clinical deterioration if untreated

questions.question: Is there any pericardial effusion (even small) on echocardiography?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — pericardial effusion in PAH confirmed; present in ~28% of PAH patients; strong independent predictor of mortality; high-risk classification regardless of size

questions.question: Is there a confirmed pathogenic variant in BMPR2, ALK1, ENG, SMAD9, CAV1, or KCNK3 on genetic testing?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — heritable PAH (HPAH) confirmed; BMPR2 variants associated with younger onset, worse hemodynamics, lower vasoreactivity response rate, and higher mortality than idiopathic PAH

questions.question: Is PAH associated with systemic sclerosis (SSc-PAH), congenital heart disease (Eisenmenger), or portal hypertension?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — high-risk PAH association confirmed; SSc-PAH has worst prognosis among CTD-PAH subtypes; Eisenmenger requires specialized management; portopulmonary PAH limits transplant eligibility

questions.question: Has the patient failed to achieve low-risk status (NT-proBNP <300 pg/mL, 6MWD >440 m, WHO FC I–II) after ≥3 months of optimized combination therapy?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes — failure to reach treatment goals confirmed; treat-to-target strategy requires escalation; sotatercept (Winrevair) consideration; lung transplant referral if triple therapy fails
